status_summary: H.R. 3174, the Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act, passed the House by voice vote under suspension on 2025-12-01 after the House Small Business Committee reported it (H. Rept. 119-224). Its engrossed text defines small manufacturers (NAICS sectors 31 to 33 with all production facilities in the United States) and adds higher 7(a) guarantee limits for them alongside the existing ones: 7.5 million dollars against the general 3.75 million, 9 million against the 4.5 million limit (with no more than 8 million for working capital, supplies or export financings), and 10 million against 5 million for export loans; it also replaces a 5.5 million dollar development company (504) limit with 10 million. In the Senate the bill was placed on the Legislative Calendar on 2025-12-04 and the Small Business and Entrepreneurship Committee held a hearing on 2026-05-13, its latest action; it is not enacted. Separately, SBA announced on 2026-05-18 a policy, effective July 4, letting borrowers who secure a 7(a) loan first combine up to 5 million dollars of 7(a) and 5 million dollars of 504 financing; neither step creates the 50 million dollar category the chapter cites.

timeline.event: The House passed H.R. 3174, the Made in America Manufacturing Finance Act, which doubles 7(a) guarantee limits for small manufacturers and raises a 504 limit to 10 million dollars.
The Senate vitiates the bill's referral to the Finance Committee and places H.R. 3174 on the Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders (Calendar No. 283).
The Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship holds a hearing on H.R. 3174, the bill's latest recorded action.

SBA announced a policy, which it called a new rule, letting borrowers who secure a 7(a) loan first combine 7(a) and 504 loans for up to 10 million dollars in total SBA-backed financing, effective July 4 (2026 inferred from the release date).
